content.rendered:
Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it. Not most things. Everything. The heart is the wellspring. What is in it eventually shows up everywhere.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, June 20, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.”
Proverbs 4:23 (NIV)

Today’s Message

In Hebrew thinking, the heart was not just the seat of feelings. The heart was the centre of the whole inner person. Mind, will, memory, intention and desire all lived in the heart. When Solomon says guard your heart, he is talking about the entire inner architecture of who you are. The thinking. The deciding. The wanting. The remembering. All of it.

And he uses one of the strongest words in the Old Testament for guarding. The Hebrew is natsar. It is the word used for keeping a vineyard from foxes, for protecting a city from invaders, for watching prisoners so they do not escape. It carries the energy of active, vigilant, deliberate protection. The heart is precious enough to require that kind of attention.

Why? Because everything you do flows from it. The Hebrew literally reads, “for from it are the outgoings of life.” The life you live outwardly is the overflow of what is happening inwardly. A guarded heart produces a life of integrity. An unguarded heart eventually produces leaks everywhere. The marriage that fails. The career that crashes. The friendship that breaks. The depression that settles in. The bitterness that hardens. These outward fractures almost always trace back to inward neglect.

What does guarding the heart look like in practice? It looks like paying attention to what you let in. The eyes are gates. The ears are gates. The mouth is a gate. The phone is a gate. The screen is a gate. The relationships you spend time with are gates. Every input you allow into your inner life either fortifies your heart or weakens it. The believer who guards the heart is not paranoid. They are simply alert. They notice what is coming in. They refuse what would harm. They welcome what would build.

And the heart is guarded most effectively not by sheer willpower but by being filled with what is good. The Word of God in the heart crowds out lies. Worship in the heart crowds out cynicism. Communion with the Spirit in the heart crowds out anxiety. The best guard for the heart is a heart that is already full of what is right. The enemy has less room to work when Christ already occupies the territory.

So above all else, today, guard your heart. Pay attention to the gates. Notice what is coming in. Refuse what would harm. Welcome what would build. Everything you do flows from this place. Tend it well.

Prayer

Father, today I guard my heart. I pay attention to what I let in through my eyes, my ears, my words, my screens and my friendships. Fill the territory of my heart with Yourself, with Your Word, with worship, and with the company of the Spirit. Crowd out what would corrupt me. Let everything that flows out of my life today be the overflow of a heart guarded for You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Above all else, I guard my heart. The Spirit of God lives in me. I am alert to what comes in. I refuse what would harm me. I welcome what would build me. Everything that flows from my life today is the overflow of a guarded heart.
